chain.label: No FAA oversight or regulatory requirements for Part 91 air tour operator
chain.trigger: With the exception of SFAR 71 pilot checkrides, the FAA performed no meaningful oversight of Bali Hai since 2002; Part 91 air tour operators are not subject to any initial or recurrent pilot-training requirements or any flight time and duty period limitations

chain.label: Pilot inexperienced in assessing Kauai weather, untrained on local patterns
chain.trigger: he began conducting tour flights after accruing just 6.7 hours of flight training from company personnel, none of which included specific training on Kauai weather

caused_by.evidence: Bali Hai was not required to have company-specific initial training; a requirement for IOE was not implemented

chain.label: Fatigued, dehydrated pilot on eighth tour after 7.7 hours at the controls without breaks
chain.trigger: he had been at the controls of the helicopter with the rotors turning for about 7.7 hours and had been observed to leave the cockpit briefly only once; passengers on the seventh tour stated that the pilot looked 'extremely tired'

caused_by.evidence: Bali Hai operated under Part 91 and was, therefore, not subject to flight time, duty period, or rest requirements

chain.label: High Kahili Ridge terrain along the tour route
chain.trigger: ATC radar data indicate that the helicopter passed over terrain elevations as high as 3,000 feet

chain.label: Advancing line of rain showers lowering cloud bases and obscuring the ridge
chain.trigger: a line of weather echoes containing rain showers was converging on the ridge near the accident location... associated with a lowering of cloud bases below 2,400 feet msl and obscuration of the higher terrain

chain.label: Decision to continue VFR south along Kahili Ridge instead of deviating east to clear weather
chain.trigger: Rather than deviate to the east, however, the pilot chose to fly south, along his usual tour route adjacent to Kahili Ridge, as the advancing line of clouds closed in on the high terrain

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's decision to fly into an area of deteriorating weather and high terrain, despite the availability of a safer route to the east, was an error that played an important causal role
the pilot's inexperience with Hawaii weather conditions affected his ability to make appropriate in-flight decisions when faced with deteriorating weather
Bali Hai's pilot-scheduling practices... likely had an adverse impact on pilot decision-making and performance

chain.label: Attempted crossing of Kahili Ridge at an off-route pass below SFAR 71 minimums, into clouds
chain.trigger: The ridge pass near the accident site was more than 1 mile from the centerline of the company's approved transition segment; therefore, any crossing at that location would have to be performed in compliance with the SFAR 71 minimum altitude of 1,500 feet agl

caused_by.evidence: the pilot had the option of avoiding these inconveniences by continuing along his usual flightpath adjacent to the Kahili Ridge and attempting to cross the ridge at the high pass
because the Honolulu FSDO is not providing direct surveillance and enforcement of SFAR 71, pilots continue to violate SFAR 71 and the certificate of waiver or authorization requirements

chain.label: Pilot spatially disoriented in prolonged IMC while in a sustained turn at high workload
chain.trigger: the helicopter's descending spiral flightpath, which became increasingly erratic in the final seconds of the flight, was consistent with pilot spatial disorientation

caused_by.evidence: the extent of the weather echoes and the duration of the sustained turn captured by the radar track suggest that the encounter with IMC was prolonged... increased the potential for spatial disorientation
visibility was dramatically reduced along the top of the ridge as the incoming line of weather reached the high terrain
any one of which would have negatively affected the pilot's concentration and decision-making

chain.label: Loss of control in an increasingly erratic clockwise spiral
chain.trigger: the erratic, zigzagging ground track that preceded the impact suggests that the pilot lost control of the helicopter before the collision

caused_by.evidence: Spatially disoriented pilots are at risk of making inappropriate control inputs that can result in loss of aircraft control

chain.label: Helicopter struck mountainous terrain on Kahili Ridge and burned
chain.trigger: impacted mountainous terrain in Kalaheo, Hawaii... the helicopter was destroyed by impact forces and postimpact fire

caused_by.evidence: when the helicopter struck the sloping terrain, it was in an extreme nose-high attitude with a high engine-power setting, neither of which are consistent with... controlled cruise or maneuvering flight
The wreckage was located on the east side of Kahili Ridge about 200 feet below the crest of the ridge at an elevation of 2,850 feet

chain.label: Pilot and four passengers fatally injured
chain.trigger: The commercial pilot and the four passengers were killed... the cause of death for each was 'multiple traumatic injuries'

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable for any of the occupants because they were subjected to impact forces that exceeded the limits of human tolerance
